name: Chaabilgish
imgNote: Illustration: a Georgian khachapuri, a close cousin. Not the Kist dish itself.
text: A Chechen-Kist flatbread, similar to khachapuri, stuffed with pumpkin and fried or griddled until blistered. A staple of the Kist table.

name: Zhizhig galnash
text: Small handmade dumpling-noodles served with boiled mutton or lamb and a garlicky broth. The signature dish of Chechen and Kist cooking.

name: Kisturi Ludi
text: A non-alcoholic Kist beer made from highland fruits and wild herbs such as rosehip and black hawthorn. Tangy and lightly fizzy, a bit like kombucha.

name: Shoti bread
text: Boat-shaped bread baked on the wall of a hot tone (clay oven). Served warm with cheese, butter and stews. The valley's maize bread is stone-ground.

name: Khinkali
text: Large twisted dumplings of spiced meat and broth. Hold by the knot, bite, sip the broth first, and leave the knot on the plate.

name: Khachapuri
text: Cheese-filled bread. The boat-shaped Adjarian version pictured is the best known, though in Kakheti you will mostly meet the round, closed imeruli style.

name: Chakapuli
text: A spring stew of lamb or veal with tarragon, sour green plums and white wine.

name: Lobio
text: Slow-cooked kidney beans with herbs and spices, typically served with corn bread (mchadi) and pickles.

name: Pkhali
text: Cold vegetable pâtés of spinach, beet or cabbage with ground walnuts, garlic and spices.

name: Fresh cheese, butter & cream
text: Valley households make their own cheeses, hand-churned butter, cream and yogurt. Sulguni, pictured, is the classic Georgian brined cheese.

name: Churchkhela
text: Walnuts strung on thread and dipped repeatedly in thickened grape or other fruit juice, then dried. A travel snack from Kakheti.
